resources.title: Ask about the past
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 4 February 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach a forty-minute lesson for three to four pupils. Reuse the invented bag and box stories from Week 3. Each pupil chooses, builds and asks one question about the past privately, then keeps the question and picture reference in a book. An unknown answer is valid.

BUILD Weekly - Spring!B44/C44: Ask a question about the past. Theme: Resilience & Change. Unit, BUILD - Spring!D10: Then & now, how things change. Term assessment, J10: F: ordering tasks.  S: personal timeline produced.

Week 5 is formative. The owner sets Week 6 as assessing. Success is an individual choice of stem and subject/detail, and a question directed to a listener. Writing or reading aloud is not required. Asking all six stems is not required.

Set Source Cards pages 1–2, Support Cards, word mat and books at each place. Starter: find torn and sewn straps in the top row. Keep the full labelled sheet. Adult may cut along white gaps and mark A–F on the reverse; pointing to the whole sheet is equally valid.

Every task keeps a word bank, sentence starters and visible model. Level 2 describes the requested scaffolds, not a qualification level. Supported, Independent and Aspire all retain these supports. Exact scribing and usual communication aids are available. No public questioning, cold calling or required reading aloud.

The objects and stories are invented teaching examples, reused unchanged from Week 3. Bag: whole strap, torn, sewn. Box: bare wood, painted, chips from use. These are supplied story clues, not real histories. No person, place, event, exact date or reason is identified. Do not invent an answer about who, where or why. “We do not know” can be an honest reply.
Thursday 4 February 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes private settle; 8 minutes find torn and sewn straps. Bank, starter and model stay visible.
5 minutes source stories with brief reset; 5 minutes model and private hinge; 5 minutes guided question build.
10 minutes ask privately and keep a book record, including brief reset; 3 minutes private review and response; 2 minutes exit and evidence.

“These objects and their stories are made up. I can see a torn strap. I want to ask what happened. My question is: What happened to the strap?” Ask a nearby adult quietly and hear the story reply. “Now choose a stem and a detail you want to ask about. You can point or ask me to write.”

Offer “What happened to the strap?” and “The strap tore.” Which asks for a reply? The first. If unsure, model asking, waiting and hearing a reply; show the stem. Parallel check: “Who sewed the strap?” asks; “The strap was sewn” tells. Do not remove the scaffolds to test memory.

Pupil selects a stem and subject/detail or offers a spontaneous question. Adult may recast grammar and read it back for keep/change. Record the pupil’s choices and all adult-supplied ideas. A directed scribe can read the confirmed question to a listener with the pupil present; record that mode. Copying the model alone is not evidence of building and asking an own question.

All sources are inside this pack. No live research, handling of actual objects or personal disclosure is needed. Adult cutting; optional touch. Offer HELP/PASS, quiet request, supported observation or an agreed supervised pause. Give quiet wait time and plan in any language.
Thursday 4 February 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: select a stem and detail, confirm the built question, then ask through speech, showing, usual aid or directed scribing. Independent: build and ask with all scaffolds. Aspire: add a different stem or explain whether a reply is known from a clue. Every route finishes with one pupil-chosen question asked privately and kept in a book.

Cognition: one picture and step at a time. Communication: short stems, wait time, usual aid and exact scribe. SEMH: predictable routine, private help and no personal disclosure. Sensory/physical: large pictures, adult cutting and optional touch. Words, letters, shape, position and borders carry meaning without colour.

Evidence HUM-BUILD-S1-W05-E1: chosen picture/clue, pupil-selected stem and detail, exact question, how it was asked, actual reply and support. Use Pupil number: ____ for each pupil; absent pupils remain blank. Record selection and asking separately. Actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode precede R. E follows actual banking. No actual results are pre-filled.

A collections worker asks questions about objects and checks clues. Offer authentic questions and choices to the Communication portfolio. Do not infer independent speech, writing or award completion from supported communication.
